notes: On the test date (2026-06-09) the Indian market was in a confirmed downtrend (Nifty below its 50-DMA, VIX spiking on Mideast/crude shock), so the correct answer to most prompts was restraint. This compressed the with-skill vs baseline pass-rate gap: strong baselines already reached cautious conclusions.

with_skill pass rate 100% (4/4 evals) vs without_skill ~89.6%. The two baseline misses were on 'applies all four gates systematically' (eval-0, eval-2) — baselines covered momentum/trend well but treated volume and per-name sentiment unevenly.

Discipline divergence is the real signal, not raw pass-rate: on eval-0 (headline) and eval-2 (watchlist) the skill returned ZERO names while baselines surfaced a conditional pick (Paras Defence; Tata Motors buy-the-dip). The skill enforced the user's 'don't give me a name' rule more strictly.

Skill caught issues baselines could miss: a STALE 'Strong Buy' data source on TCS (eval-2) and a binary NCLT demerger-EGM event landmine on Apollo (eval-1). The sentiment gate's event-awareness is pulling weight.
Cost of rigor: with_skill averaged ~219s and ~46k tokens vs ~186s and ~33k for baseline (+33s, +13k tokens). The extra spend buys systematic four-gate coverage and event/data-quality checks.

Caveat: single run per cell, and assertions are process/discipline checks (stock picks vary daily), so pass-rate is a coarse instrument here — the qualitative outputs matter more than the numbers this iteration.
